data.narrative:
BurnBot is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Anukool Lakhina and Waleed Haddad that has raised $25M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises nine private climate and energy firms, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

Valuation triangulation relied on a single applicable method due to peer-set constraints. Stage-progression analysis, using the $25M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielded an implied valuation of $50M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while nine same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage-adjacent or similar-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints, making a narrow peer multiple unreliable. An all-sector median would introduce excessive noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M (low) to $57M (high), centered on $50M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and the absence of tight peer anchors at identical stage and capital structure. Key uncertainties include whether the 2.0x Series A step-up assumption appropriately reflects BurnBot's specific risk profile relative to climate-tech peers, and whether materializing a larger peer dataset—or access to recent Series A round terms for comparable firms—would materially shift the implied multiple.
